Maintenance Report — MNT-0082-007

Asset: WELL-0082 (SW-24 Well 082, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 10 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 14 Feb 2024 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 89 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0082-0067 on 2024-02-08 Report written: 16 Feb 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0082-0067 showed the wellhead at 7.9 °C with the air at 5.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,381
Bolts, shims and seals345
Bearing grease and consumables575
Labour (company crew)1,763
Total4,064

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 4 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0082-010

Asset: WELL-0082 (SW-24 Well 082, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 26 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 01 May 2024 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 122 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0082-0077 on 2024-04-25 Report written: 01 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0082-0077 showed the wellhead at 23.3 °C with the air at 23.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 3 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level; one crew member's monitor had not been bump-tested that day (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Sucker rods2,748
Rod couplings687
Fishing tool rental1,145
Labour (company crew and contractor)5,217
Total9,797

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03Not metOne monitor not bump-tested that day
WS-07MetWritten the same day as the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.
  • HSE to follow up on the WS-03 item above with the crew.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0082-011

Asset: WELL-0082 (SW-24 Well 082, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 17 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 04 Jun 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 428 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0082-0080 on 2024-05-16 Report written: 05 Jun 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0082-0080 showed the wellhead at 30.1 °C with the air at 26.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 16 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0082-012

Asset: WELL-0082 (SW-24 Well 082, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 08 Jun 2024 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 24 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0082-0083 on 2024-06-06 Report written: 09 Jun 2024

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0082-0083 at 09:00 on 2024-06-06 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.3% of the pad area, estimated 2.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 260 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 208 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0082-012 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.37% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
